title: Business Operations Manager - DTC
description:
At Wyze, we make smart home technology accessible to everyone. We're known for disrupting markets with high-quality, affordable products - from cameras to lighting to sensors and more. We believe technology should simplify life, not complicate it. We’re a fast-moving, customer-obsessed team driven by curiosity and powered by data.
The Opportunity
Wyze is hiring a Business Operations Manager to own the commercial performance of our direct-to-consumer business in North America, including wyze.com in the US and Canada. You will own pricing, promotions, assortment, and bundles across the full Wyze product portfolio. You will be accountable for revenue, promotion efficiency, and contribution profit against plan.
Your vendors are Wyze's own product lines. You will represent the DTC channel to Product, Sales, Finance, and Services. You will negotiate for the offers, launch timing, and selection that grow the channel, and work with Product to bring DTC-specific products and bundles to market.
This is a business owner role. The job requires a lot of analysis, but the goal is to make decisions and deliver results.
What You’ll Do
Own the DTC portfolio P&L levers for North America: gross revenue, net revenue, promotion spend and ROI against plan
Report against and partner with cross-functional teams on contribution profit against plan
Build the unit and revenue plan with the Head of E-commerce and own the DTC demand forecast by SKU
Set DTC prices within company pricing guidelines. Align with Sales and Finance on national promotional pricing and price matching
Own the promotion calendar: what to promote, when, at what depth, and how to measure incremental impact
Manage assortment across new launches, core products, accessories, and end-of-life SKUs. Work with Product to develop DTC-specific products
Design bundles, kits, and attach offers that grow order value and profit, including subscriptions sold on DTC
Run a weekly business review that explains what happened, why, and which actions close the gap to plan
Partner with Inventory Planning, Merchandising, Marketing, Site Development, and Customer Service to turn decisions into execution
What You’ll Bring
Bachelor’s degree in business or related field
4+ years of experience in vendor management, category management, ecommerce, retail, or related commercial role
Experience owning revenue and margin targets, with direct decisions on pricing, promotions, or assortment
Fluency in unit economics: gross and net revenue, COGS, promotion cost, and contribution profit
A track record of using data to find the highest-value lever, make a decision, and measure the result
Experience influencing cross-functional partners and senior leaders without direct authority
Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills. Comfortable with SQL or BI tools
Clear, concise writing and the ability to explain tradeoffs in plain terms
Helpful, But Not Required
MBA preferred
Experience in consumer electronics, smart home, or hardware with subscription services
Amazon vendor management or DTC ecommerce experience, ideally on Shopify
Experience with demand forecasting, price elasticity, or promotion analytics
Experience building bundle, kit, or attach programs
Compensation
The base pay range for this role is $113,000 – $140,000 per year.

title: Data Scientist ll
description:
At Wyze, we make smart home technology accessible to everyone. We're known for disrupting markets with high-quality, affordable products - from cameras to lighting to sensors and more. We believe technology should simplify life, not complicate it. We’re a fast-moving, customer-obsessed team driven by curiosity and powered by data.
We're looking for a Data Scientist to help improve the quality, organization, and usability of the data that powers our AI/ML products. This isn't a reporting or dashboarding role — you'll be training, updating, and running models directly against large-scale datasets, diagnosing systemic quality issues, and building the frameworks that determine what data is fit for training. You'll work at the intersection of applied machine learning, data quality engineering, and analytical tooling.
What You'll Do
Assess and structure training data: Evaluate large-scale datasets for quality, apply structured labeling frameworks, and diagnose systemic gaps or inconsistencies that affect model performance
Train, update, and apply models against existing data: Train or fine-tune models, apply scoring/classification tools against datasets to auto-tier or flag quality at scale, and iterate on models as new data or requirements emerge
Surface insights: Explore labeling and usage patterns to find where data quality is strong or weak, and turn findings into clear, defensible recommendations
Support data pipeline integration: Partner with engineers to ensure clean, well-labeled data flows smoothly into downstream systems and model training workflows
Test and validate: Validate model outputs and quality-scoring results against ground truth before they're used downstream, and monitor for drift or regressions as data and models evolve
Contribute to tooling improvements: Provide input on internal tools used for data labeling and review, helping shape what they need to track, automate, or support
Build quality frameworks: Define metrics and benchmarks that answer “how good is our data?” and track them over time, with a direct eye toward how data quality impacts model performance
What We're Looking For
Master's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field
1–4 years of experience in data science, machine learning, or a related quantitative field
Solid understanding of machine learning fundamentals — how training data quality affects model performance, common failure modes from bad/biased data, and how to evaluate a model's output critically
Hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or updating ML models — not just applying pre-built tools or doing descriptive analysis
Strong SQL and Python skills (pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, or a deep learning framework such as PyTorch/TensorFlow); comfortable exploring and cleaning large, messy datasets independently
Practical experience working with AI coding tools (e.g., Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, or similar) as part of your daily workflow, with an agentic mindset — comfortable delegating well-scoped subtasks to AI tools/agents, verifying their output, and iterating quickly rather than hand-coding everything from scratch
Ability to translate ambiguous questions into measurable, trackable metrics
Familiarity with data labeling or annotation workflows is a plus, not required
A quality-first, curious mindset — interested in why data issues occur, not just flagging them
Exposure to computer vision or video/image datasets specifically is a plus
Success Looks Like
Measurable improvement in data quality and coverage over time
Clear, trusted quality benchmarks that inform data and modeling decisions
Strong collaboration with engineering on data pipeline health
Base Salary range of $121,000 - $150,000 DOE + bonus target up to 20% + equity
Compensation
The base pay range for this role is $121,000 – $150,000 per year.
